name: PINOCHLE TWO PLAYER
description: Pinochle for two players. Melding and trick-taking with 48-card deck; two-player rules (e.g. dummy hand or special deal).

content.text: Pinochle for two players. Melding and trick-taking with 48-card deck; two-player rules (e.g. dummy hand or special deal).

Pinochle is derived from bezique and is related to Binokel (Binocle), which developed in Switzerland and South Germany. German immigrants brought Binokel to America in the last quarter of the 19th century, where it was mispronounced and misspelled as pinochle. It became a favorite of American Jewish and Irish immigrants. The two-player form uses the same 48-card deck and follows the same meld-and-trick structure: bidding, melding, then trick play adapted for two hands. During World War I some US cities briefly outlawed pinochle due to anti-German sentiment; it has since regained popularity.
48 cards (two copies of 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace in each of four suits).

Deal twelve cards to each player in packets of four; 24 cards remain as stock. In bidding variants, bid winner may declare trump then both lay melds; in classic variant, players draw one card from stock after each of the first twelve tricks and may meld after winning a trick.
